gates.evidence: Mainnet chain/RPC/explorer/token/CCTP values are intentionally unset in the release.

No independent final audit sign-off is recorded. An in-house 3-way parallel self-review (market/AMM contracts, lending/agent-economy contracts, frontend revert-risk/UX) ran 2026-07-27 and found no critical/high exploitable issue; every medium-severity finding it surfaced was fixed and redeployed the same day (see docs/ARCODIAN-AUDIT-READINESS.md). A self-review is not a substitute for third-party sign-off.
A 2-of-2 governance canary is live at 0x4EA3...a3aa, but legacy immutable fee recipients still point to treasury EOA and a final mainnet signer policy is not approved.
ArcLendV2 (0x571493d3...65d, redeployed 2026-07-27) admin is timelock 0x4e15...AaCD; emergency guardian is separate 0xc406...3c75 and cannot override oracle or withdraw reserves.

Cap decreases are immediate for guardian/admin; increases require a 24-hour timelock action plus an intrinsic 48-hour market delay. Caps raised 2026-07-27 from an under-sized 100/50 USDC canary to 50,000/25,000 USDC — same governed mechanism, larger ceiling; this specific number has not itself had an external sign-off.

100% complete 2026-07-27: all 27 canonical addresses in public/developers/contracts.json are deployed AND source-verified on Arcscan/Blockscout (public/developers/verification-status.json), once the outage from 2026-07-22 through 2026-07-26 resolved. Regenerate with `node scripts/verify-canonical-contracts.mjs`; the exact forge verify-contract invocation for every contract is documented in contracts/DEPLOYMENT.md.
Indexers, monitor, and public feeds are healthy but run on one host.
Keeper and analytics preflight multiple RPC transports, but a second independent signer/host is not configured.

Official Arc Testnet Pyth deployment, 1% confidence guard, 20% deviation breaker are active. Freshness window changed 2026-07-27 from a hardcoded 1 hour to a per-market immutable maxOracleAge (90 hours for the live EUR/USD market) — the 1-hour bound was itself a bug: EUR/USD is a traditional-FX Pyth feed that only publishes during NY market hours and goes fully silent the whole weekend, so a 1-hour window falsely reverted OracleStale() every Friday close through Sunday reopen regardless of oracle health. The wider window is a deliberate tradeoff (weekend-safe vs. slower detection of a genuinely broken feed on a weekday) that an independent auditor should confirm explicitly, not inherit from this line.

50,000 USDC supply / 25,000 USDC borrow caps (raised 2026-07-27 from 100/50 USDC canary); live supply-collateral-borrow-repay-withdraw E2E completed with zero bad debt on the current ArcLendV2 deployment, with utilization/rate response verified against the exact curve formula.

Agent Pay factory has isolated immutable-owner vaults and no factory admin path into vault funds. ArcAgentPayV4 (2026-07-27) additionally requires the vault owner to still be an agentId's CURRENT Identity Registry owner at both setPolicy and payInvoice, closing a staleness gap where a resold agentId's stale passport binding could keep spending a previous owner's vault; live-confirmed against a real, externally-owned agentId. Prior V3 vaults are unaffected and keep working.

ArcAgentJobsV2 (redeployed 2026-07-27) now rejects job creation if the evaluator equals the client or the provider (SelfDealing()), closing a self-dealing hole where a client could unilaterally reject legitimate work or a provider could self-approve. Live-confirmed both the revert and that a normal 3-party job still succeeds.

ArcAdminTimelock (redeployed 2026-07-27) changed transferAdmin from a single unchecked step (no zero-address guard, a typo permanently bricked admin control) to a two-step propose/accept plus a separate explicit renounceAdmin. Live-proven both halves: a burn-address proposal left admin untouched and unacceptable by anyone, then a real propose->accept round-trip succeeded.

Unified monitoring and Pyth keeper timers are active and enabled. A 2026-07-27 systemd-wide sweep found 6 of these services (analytics/treasury/fx-stats/arcpay-stats/agentpay-index/monitor) had been silently failing on EVERY scheduled run since inception — each called an npm script that never existed in package.json — leaving their public data files frozen for roughly 2 days with zero error surfaced anywhere. All 6 fixed (pointed directly at their real scripts, matching the pattern the working indexers already used) and verified producing fresh output within seconds of the fix. A 7th bug (fx-stats.mjs had no checkpointing, so a full historical rescan could never finish inside its own timeout and looped forever) was fixed with the same incremental-checkpoint pattern arcpay-stats.mjs already used.
Mainnet deployment remains disabled unless every explicit release variable and sign-off is supplied.
